template/basic.cpp: Replace the dollar-brace cursor placeholder and date variables. Add cassert when using assertions on newer GCC. With LOCAL, the debug include expects algo/debug.h on the include path.
Replace ${0}; write the solution inside main().
data/dsu.cpp: Vertices are 0-based, but Min/Max store labels 1..n. Change both iota starts to 0 when you want vertex IDs.
DSU d(n); d.unite(u, v); bool same = d.same(u, v);
data/rollback_dsu.cpp: snapshot() returns a history position. Roll back only to a previous snapshot; failed unions create no history.
RollbackDSU d(n); int s = d.snapshot(); d.unite(u, v); d.rollback(s);
data/fenwick.cpp: 1-based inclusive prefixes. For N elements construct with N+1. Never modify index 0: lowbit(0)=0 causes an infinite loop.
FenwickTree<long long> f(n + 1); f.modify(i, x); auto sum = f.query(r);
data/fenwick2d.cpp: O(log n log m) per op
1-based inclusive queries. For N by M elements construct with N+1,M+1. Both update indices must be positive.
FenwickTree2D<long long> f(n + 1, m + 1); f.modify(x, y, val);
data/segtree.cpp: Point assignment; query [l,r). Original identity and initial values are 0: assumes nonnegative values. For negatives, use LLONG_MIN in both tree initialization and query accumulator.
Segtree st(n); st.modify(i, x); auto best = st.query(l, r);
data/lazy_segtree.cpp: 0-based [l,r). Initially zero; add(i,i+1,a[i]) initializes an element. Updates and queries use 128-bit intermediates. Stored node sums, lazy tags, and final query answers must fit signed 64-bit.
LazySegtree st(n); st.add(l, r, x); auto sum = st.query(l, r);
data/persistent_segtree.cpp: 0-based [l,r). Save each returned root; older roots remain valid. Difference of two roots gives frequency/range differences. Root 0 is all zero.
PersistentSegtree st(n); int root = st.add(0, i, x); auto sum = st.query(root, l, r);
data/sparsetable.cpp: O(n log n) build, O(1) query
Nonempty input. get(l,r) is inclusive. Operation must be associative and idempotent (min, max, gcd), not sum.
auto f = [](int x, int y) { return min(x, y); }; SparseTable st(a, f); st.get(l, r);
data/pbds.cpp: GNU libstdc++ extension. find_by_order(k) is 0-based; order_of_key(x) counts keys strictly below x. For duplicates use pair(value,unique_id).
ordered_set<int> s; s.insert(x); auto it = s.find_by_order(k);
data/custom_hash.cpp: Example: unordered_map<long long,int,custom_hash>. Reserve capacity and consider max_load_factor(0.7).
unordered_map<long long, int, custom_hash> mp; mp.reserve(n);
graph/bfs.cpp: Unweighted graph, 0-based adjacency list. Unreachable distances are -1.
graph/zero_one_bfs.cpp: Weights must be exactly 0 or 1. Unreachable distance is INT_MAX.
graph/dijkstra.cpp: Nonnegative weights only. Unreachable is 4e18. Distances and d+w must fit long long and remain below this sentinel.
graph/bellman_ford.cpp: Negative edges allowed. neg[v] means distance is unbounded below. Only cycles reachable from s count; finite distances are valid when neg[v] is false. Keep n*sum(abs(w)) well below 4e18.
graph/floyd_warshall.cpp: Initialize to 4e18, diagonal 0, and minimum parallel-edge weights. If d[k][k]<0, pairs reaching and leaving k have no finite shortest path.
floyd_warshall(d); // d is the initialized distance matrix
graph/toposort.cpp: Kahn's algorithm; an empty result indicates a cycle unless V=0. DAG DP follows this order.
graph/scc.cpp: Iterative Kosaraju avoids recursion depth. IDs run from sources to sinks: for every edge u->v, comp[u]<=comp[v].
graph/two_sat.cpp: DEPENDENCY: graph/scc.cpp. Literal 2*v means false, 2*v+1 means true; xor 1 negates it. either(a,b) adds (a OR b); implication a=>b is either(a^1,b).
TwoSAT sat(n); sat.either(2 * x + 1, 2 * y); bool ok = sat.solve();
graph/bridges.cpp: Undirected graph; parallel edges and self-loops supported. Call run once after adding all edges. bridge[id] and cut[v] are outputs. Recursive DFS: watch stack on long chains.
graph/kruskal.cpp: DEPENDENCY: data/dsu.cpp. Handles negative weights and disconnected graphs. A spanning tree uses exactly n-1 edges (for n>=1).
graph/lca.cpp: O(V log V) build, O(log V) query
Connected nonempty tree, 0-based. Recursive construction can overflow the stack on a long chain. Distance(a,b)=depth[a]+depth[b]-2*depth[get(a,b)].
LCA tree(g, root); int ancestor = tree.get(u, v);
graph/hld.cpp: Connected nonempty tree. Combine with a segment tree: path(a,b,[&](int l,int r){...}). For sums/min/max, order does not matter; directional/noncommutative queries need extra handling. Subtrees are contiguous.
HLD h(g); h.path(u, v, [&](int l, int r) { /* query [l,r) */ });
graph/virtual_tree.cpp: O(k log k + k log n)

DEPENDENCY: graph/hld.cpp. Compress k marked vertices and their LCAs from a connected tree. Duplicates are removed. vertex maps local to original IDs; parent and g use local IDs. Directed edges store original edge counts. Empty marks give an empty tree; otherwise root is local 0, with at most 2k-1 vertices.
graph/euler_trail.cpp: Given start s, returns edge IDs or nullopt. Supports parallel edges and loops. Empty-edge graph has a valid empty trail. For an open trail choose the vertex with out-in=1.
graph/dinic.cpp: Nonnegative integral capacities; total flow fits long long. add(u,v,c) creates a directed edge. Add both directions for an undirected capacity edge. After flow, level[v]>=0 identifies the source side of a minimum cut. Recursive blocking-flow DFS.
Dinic f(n); f.add(u, v, cap); auto value = f.flow(s, t);
graph/mincost_flow.cpp: Simple Bellman-Ford version favors clarity over speed. Negative costs OK, but no negative-cost residual cycles. Costs/distances/products must fit long long and stay below 4e18. Returned flow may be less than need.
MinCostFlow f(n); f.add(u, v, cap, cost); auto result = f.run(s, t, need);
graph/hopcroft_karp.cpp: Left vertices 0..n-1, right 0..m-1. g[left] stores right IDs. left/right are partners or -1. Recursive augmenting DFS. For a minimum vertex cover use alternating reachability from unmatched left vertices.
HopcroftKarp hk(n, m); hk.g[u].push_back(v); int size = hk.run();
graph/hungarian.cpp: Dense n by m signed-cost matrix. Assigns every row to a distinct column, returning (minimum cost, row-to-column matching), or nullopt if n>m. Empty input has cost 0. Potentials use __int128; the final total must fit signed 64-bit. For maximum weight, transform costs within range.
string/z_function.cpp: z[0]=n in this implementation. For pattern search use pattern + separator + text, with a separator absent from both strings.
string/prefix_kmp.cpp: Returns 0-based match starts, including overlaps. Empty pattern matches all text boundaries.
string/manacher.cpp: odd[i] includes the center; even[i] is centered between i-1 and i. Longest lengths are 2*odd[i]-1 and 2*even[i]. Total palindromic substrings = sum(odd)+sum(even).
string/aho_corasick.cpp: Lowercase a-z, nonempty patterns. Add every pattern, build exactly once, then count. Counts overlapping occurrences and duplicate patterns. out stores counts, not pattern IDs.
AhoCorasick ac; ac.add(pattern); ac.build(); auto total = ac.count(text);
string/suffix_array.cpp: O(n log^2 n) build, O(n) LCP
Byte strings, no sentinel required; empty input supported. lcp[i]=LCP(sa[i],sa[i+1]). LCP of suffix ranks a<b is min(lcp[a..b-1]); use a sparse table. Distinct substrings=n*(n+1)/2-sum(lcp).
string/suffix_automaton.cpp: Lowercase a-z. Extend in text order. distinct() counts distinct nonempty substrings; occurrence counts require extra propagation in descending state length.
SuffixAutomaton sam; for (char c : s) { sam.extend(c); } sam.distinct();
string/min_rotation.cpp: Booth algorithm. Returns the smallest 0-based start of a lexicographically minimum rotation, comparing unsigned bytes. Empty input returns 0. The rotated string is s.substr(i)+s.substr(0,i).
numeric/fastpow.cpp: Original accepts int base/exponent/modulus. Use nonnegative base and exponent, modulus>=2; normalize negative bases before calling. Negative exponents do not terminate.
numeric/extgcd.cpp: For nonnegative a,b, returns g with a*x+b*y=g. At least one input must be positive for meaningful inversion. Coefficient intermediates must fit T.
long long x, y; auto g = extgcd(a, b, x, y);
numeric/mint.cpp: Replace the dollar-brace modulus placeholder. Prefer Type=int with modulus<=1e9+9; the long long multiplication branch can overflow signed arithmetic. Division requires gcd(divisor,mod)=1. Inverse uses assert, which disappears under NDEBUG. Commented combinatorics helpers are optional.
Mint x = 3; Mint y = power(x, 10); // set md first
numeric/sieve.cpp: spf[x] is the smallest prime factor; phi is Euler's totient, mu is Mobius. factor(x) requires 1<=x<=n. Memory about 12*n bytes plus prime list.
numeric/crt.cpp: Solves x=a mod m and x=b mod n, even for noncoprime moduli. Returns normalized (x,lcm) or nullopt. Positive moduli; merged lcm must fit signed 64-bit. Uses __int128 intermediates.
auto solution = crt_merge(a, m, b, n);
numeric/combinatorics.cpp: Prime MOD, precomputation limit n<MOD. Example: Combinations<1000000007> c(N); c.C(n,k). n must be precomputed; invalid k returns 0.
Combinations<1000000007> c(n); auto ways = c.C(n, k);
numeric/miller_rabin.cpp: Seven witness bases cover all uint64_t inputs; unsigned __int128 prevents multiplication overflow. pow_mod needs nonzero modulus.
numeric/pollard_rho.cpp: DEPENDENCY: numeric/miller_rabin.cpp. factor64(n,out) for n>=1; sort output to group prime powers. This simple Floyd-cycle variant may be slow on hard semiprimes; runtime is not guaranteed.
vector<u64> factors; factor64(n, factors); sort(factors.begin(), factors.end());
numeric/ntt.cpp: Namespace NTT; coefficients normalized mod 998244353. Padded length must be <=2^23. This is modular convolution; integer convolution needs coefficient bounds or multiple primes plus CRT.
numeric/berlekamp_massey.cpp: Prime MOD. Returns shortest coefficients c consistent with s sample terms: a[n]=sum(c[j]*a[n-1-j]). To recover a sequence with known order bound d, supply at least 2d terms. Empty/all-zero samples return empty. Use the nth-term helper to extrapolate.
numeric/linear_recurrence.cpp: Nth term of a linear recurrence

c[j] multiplies a[n-1-j]. initial must contain exactly d=c.size() initial terms a[0..d-1]. Returns the 0-based kth term modulo MOD>=2; composite moduli supported. Empty recurrence means the zero sequence. Accepts uint64_t k.
numeric/gauss.cpp: Nonempty augmented real matrix. Returns 0/1/2 for none/unique/infinite. Free variables are set to 0. Absolute EPS=1e-9; adjust for scale. Do not use for exact modular equations.
vector<double> x; int status = gauss(augmented, x);
numeric/gauss_binary.cpp: Equations over GF(2), m<=MAXV variables. Each bitset<MAXV+1> row holds coefficients in bits 0..m-1 and RHS in bit m. Returns rank or -1 if inconsistent. Free variables are zero; solution is unique iff rank==m. Bits above m are ignored.
bitset<512> x; int rank = gauss_binary<512>(rows, m, x);
geometry/integer_geometry.cpp: Hull O(n log n), polygon test O(n)
Coordinates |x|,|y|<=1e9. Cross products and doubled area use __int128. Hull is CCW and omits collinear interior points. Polygon must be simple; point test returns -1/0/1 outside/boundary/inside.
auto hull = convex_hull(points); auto twice_area = area2(hull);
geometry/closest_pair.cpp: O(n log n) time, O(n) space

DEPENDENCY: geometry/integer_geometry.cpp. Coordinates |x|,|y|<=1e9. Returns (exact squared distance, original index, original index); nullopt for fewer than two points. Duplicate points are supported. Any optimum pair may be returned.
geometry/polygon_diameter.cpp: DEPENDENCY: geometry/integer_geometry.cpp. Strict CCW convex hull, with no repeated endpoint, such as convex_hull output. Coordinates |x|,|y|<=1e9. Returns (exact squared distance, hull index, hull index). Empty input returns nullopt; one point has distance 0.
auto hull = convex_hull(points); auto farthest = polygon_diameter(hull);
geometry/floating_geometry.cpp: Namespace Geo, long double. Adjust absolute EPS to scale. Lines need distinct defining points; radii nonnegative. Circle nullopt means infinitely many intersections, empty vector means none.
auto p = Geo::line_intersection(a, b, c, d);
geometry/min_enclosing_circle.cpp: DEPENDENCY: geometry/floating_geometry.cpp. Randomized incremental algorithm in namespace Geo, using long double. Returns center and radius, or nullopt for empty input. Duplicate and collinear points are supported. Containment uses EPS*max(1,radius); adjust tolerance to input scale.
dp/lis.cpp: Returns original indices. Strictly increasing; upper_bound gives nondecreasing. Empty input returns empty.
dp/li_chao.cpp: Li Chao tree on compressed coordinates
Known nonempty coordinate set, |a|,|b|,|x|<=1e18. Arbitrary insertion and query order. Minimum of a*x+b, with __int128 outputs; empty tree returns INF. Useful for dp[i]=min_j(dp[j]+a[j]*x[i]).
LiChao st(xs); st.add(a, b); auto best = st.query(x);
dp/subset_transforms.cpp: Array size must be a positive power of 2. Inverse subtracts contributions. Sum over all submasks is O(3^b) across all masks; transform is O(b*2^b).
misc/int128_io.cpp: Use cout << to_string128(value). Includes the minimum signed value safely.
misc/rng.cpp: Use uniform_int_distribution<long long>(lo,hi)(rng) for an inclusive unbiased range. Fix the seed while debugging.
misc/pragma.cpp: Check the contest compiler before enabling. CPU target pragmas may produce illegal instructions on another machine.
misc/fastinput.cpp: Original template, preserved unchanged. Macro replaces cin; do not mix with iostream input. Uses signed-char EOF; floating extraction expects double. Integer parsing uses a positive magnitude. Character extraction leaves the lookahead unchanged. EOF-controlled token loops need trailing whitespace after the final token.
int n; cin >> n; // include the original input snippet first
misc/fastoutput.cpp: Original template, preserved unchanged. Macro replaces cout. Signed integer formatting requires representable negation; floating formatting expects double (float is promoted). No endl/iomanip support. Flushes on destruction. When combined with the original input template, remove cin.tie(nullptr), because its tie stub takes int.
cout << answer << '\n'; // include the original output snippet first
debug.h: Include for local debugging. Prefer the starter's disabled debug macro in submissions. Generic container formatting needs iterable values; avoid name collisions with other to_string overloads.
debug(a, b); // with LOCAL and the starter debug macro
